title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
oneLinerQuestion: Design a class that processes stream numbers and continuously maintains the kth largest element.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Kth Largest Element in an Array problem asks us to find the k-th largest element in an unsorted array. While sorting the entire array takes O(N log N) time, we can achieve optimal performance using a Min-Heap. By maintaining a Min-Heap capped strictly at a maximum size of k, we ensure that the heap holds only the k largest elements seen so far. The smallest among these k elements—which naturally sits at the root of the Min-Heap—acts as the boundary threshold: any incoming element smaller than the root is discarded, while larger elements replace the root. This guarantees that upon processing all array elements, the root of the heap holds the exact k-th largest number.

- Step 1: Min-Heap Initialization — We initialize an empty Min-Heap data structure (`minHeap = new MinPriorityQueue()`) to dynamically track the top k largest values.

- Step 2: Linear Stream Traversal — We iterate through each element `num` in the input array `nums` from index `0` to `nums.length - 1`.

- Step 3: Heap Insertion — We push the current element into the min-heap: `minHeap.enqueue(num)`.

- Step 4: Size Cap Enforcement — After insertion, if the heap size exceeds k (`minHeap.size() > k`), we immediately remove the smallest element by popping the root: `minHeap.dequeue()`. This maintains the heap size strictly at k, discarding elements that cannot be part of the top k largest.

- Step 5: Heap Invariant Maintenance — Because the heap is capped at size k, the root element (`minHeap.front()`) is always greater than or equal to any elements that were evicted, representing the precise threshold of the top k elements.

- Step 6: Termination & Root Retrieval — Once all elements in `nums` have been processed, the root of the min-heap holds the k-th largest element. We return `minHeap.front().element` (or equivalent top value).

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N log k) where N is the length of `nums`, since each of the N insertions/deletions operates on a heap of maximum size k. Space Complexity: O(k) auxiliary space to maintain the bounded Min-Heap of size k.
pseudoCode:
CLASS KthLargest:
    CONSTRUCTOR(k, nums):
        minHeap = MinHeap(nums), kVal = k
        WHILE SIZE(minHeap) > kVal DO POP(minHeap)
    FUNCTION add(val):
        PUSH val TO minHeap
        IF SIZE(minHeap) > kVal THEN POP(minHeap)
        RETURN TOP(minHeap)
END CLASS

steps.narration: Lines 3-4: Constructor with k = 3, nums = [4, 5, 8, 2]. Push to minHeap and pop excess smallest (2) to maintain size 3.
Line 6: add(3): Push 3 into minHeap -> heap becomes [3, 4, 5, 8] with size 4.
Line 7: Heap size exceeds k (4 > 3). POP smallest element: 3. minHeap returns to [4, 5, 8].
Line 8: Return TOP(minHeap) = 4. The 3rd largest element is 4.
Line 6: add(5): Push 5 into minHeap -> heap becomes [4, 5, 5, 8] with size 4.
Line 7: Heap size exceeds k (4 > 3). POP smallest element: 4. minHeap becomes [5, 5, 8].
Line 8: Return TOP(minHeap) = 5. The 3rd largest element is now 5.
Line 6: add(10): Push 10 into minHeap -> heap becomes [5, 5, 8, 10] with size 4.
Line 7: Heap size exceeds k (4 > 3). POP smallest element: 5. minHeap becomes [5, 8, 10].
Line 8: Stream operations finished. Return TOP(minHeap) = 5 as the 3rd largest element.
